chapter_theme: The knower (போதன்): soul and Siva are not two, and once the soul knows Siva it remains as Siva; the knower, taught the thirty-six tattvas by Nandi's grace, passes beyond them, while those who do not know the impurities pursue hair-tearing austerities, and those busy only in the Lord's daily work miss his daily grace.

2017.reading: There is no difference called soul and Siva; souls do not know Siva, and once souls know Siva, souls remain as Siva.
2017.nuance: One of the best-known verses of the Tirumanthiram. It can be read as identity (the soul is Siva, unaware of it) or, as Siddhanta reads it, as non-separation in which the freed soul becomes Siva-like without ceasing to be; the verse uses both வேறில்லை and ஆயிட்டு இருப்பர், which pull in each direction.

2018.reading: The dancing Lord, the lamp of qualities, is the overseeing witness, a lamp in the eye, for all abiding souls whose lamp is the mind, as the many-headed serpent's lamp is the jewel in its hood.
2018.nuance: The verse stacks four lamps (குண, மன, பண, கண விளக்கு), and how they relate is not fixed. பணவிளக்கு is the jewel the serpent is said to carry in its hood. கண்காணி is an overseer or witness.

2019.reading: The knower who, being knowledge, is freed of ignorance, whose sense-doors are closed and who is himself everywhere, knows as knowledge within them all, and is also that soul which stood gathered in.
2019.nuance: போதன் may be the freed soul or the Lord, and the verse's subject shifts; பொறிவாய் ஒழிந்து (the doors of the senses ceasing) and செறிவாகி (concentrated, or densely present) carry the sense.

2020.reading: To me, who did not know the nature of the thirty-six, Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six; after I knew it by his grace, he stood beyond the thirty-six.
2020.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the thirty-six tattvas. நின்றானே is third person, so the one beyond them is Nandi; some take it of the knower, who passes beyond them with him.

2021.reading: Those who do not stand in and know the grace that is Siva, and do not know what the five ruinous impurities are, perform austerities and tear out their hair; they never seek the new truth.
2021.nuance: தலைப்பறிகின்றார் (they pluck the hair from their heads) is traditionally taken as aimed at Jain ascetics. மலம் ஐந்து is a fivefold count of impurities; நவமான தத்துவம் may be 'new', 'excellent' or 'ninefold' tattva.

2022.reading: Those who live daily in the work the Lord carries on do not daily seek the Lord's loving nourishment; since the Lord gives grace daily to the good, those who do not seek it daily are mere day-labourers.
2022.nuance: Every line begins நாடோறும் (daily), and நாடிடார், நாடார் play on நாடு (seek). நாள்வினையாளர் may be day-labourers or those bound to each day's deeds. Who 'lives in the Lord's work' is unclear: all beings, or ritual workers.

links.note: 1924 counts the thirty-six tattvas; 2020 says the count is learned from Nandi by grace and is the step to standing beyond them.

Both judge outward ascetic marks worthless without inner change: the Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what is condemned (Parimelazhagar counts hair-plucking under shaving); Tirumular says hair-tearers do not know the impurities or grace.

source_issues: 2021 line 4: நவமான is ambiguous between 'new' and 'ninefold'.
